text:
Marat Khusnutdinov scored in Boston's 6-4 win over San Jose on Oct. 24 and hasn't recorded a point since: nine straight games, as the Bruins have dropped their last three. The worrying part is that our numbers can't blame bad luck. He's had about 3 expected points of chances in that stretch, and the looks have thinned out rather than piled up unconverted.

Over the full season he has 3 goals and 6 points in 21 games on 14 minutes a night, and Boston gets about 54% of the expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, a decent mark that says his shifts aren't the problem defensively. He's quick, with his bursts over 20 mph in the top 15% of the league, but his shot is soft, near the bottom fifth by speed, so he needs to get close to score.

Last season was his best: Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins, 79th among forwards, mostly from even-strength offense, with 33 points. The 24-year-old has done this before. What to watch is whether his ice time holds while the points don't come.
